stem:
A small steel sphere is oscillating vertically on the end of a spring, as shown in Fig. 4.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The velocity *v* of the sphere varies with displacement *x* from its equilibrium position according to

*v* = ± 9.7√(11.6 − *x*²)

where *v* is in cm s⁻¹ and *x* is in cm.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the frequency of the oscillations.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the amplitude of the oscillations is 3.4 cm.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the maximum acceleration *a*₀ of the sphere.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
On Fig. 4.2, sketch the variation with *x* of the acceleration *a* of the sphere.

[[fig:f2]]

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Describe, without calculation, the interchange between the potential energy and the kinetic energy of the oscillations.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.1
figures.alt: A steel sphere hangs from a vertical spring, with a vertical double arrow indicating its oscillations and labels pointing to the spring and sphere.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.2
figures.alt: A square graph grid with horizontal axis x / cm from −4 to 4 and vertical acceleration axis a marked from −2a₀ to 2a₀.
